items.html:
The strongest existing accuracy plots can use four distinct evidence types: 70-digit reference error, analytic-zero cancellation, physical conservation residuals, and measured cutoff sensitivity. All values below come from saved artifacts; their build fingerprints should remain visible.

  1. High-precision value and derivative error: fractional-legendre-physical.json

    Schema: precision_digits, native_sha256, cases, finite_cases, max_relative_error, and results[] containing: degree, order, argument, actual=[value, derivative], reference=[decimal_string, decimal_string], expected_overflow, relative_error.

    It contains 530 finite cases against 70-digit hypergeometric references, eight degrees through 127.2, and seven arguments including ±0.999999. Maximum recorded relative error is 2.1689e-13. The metric takes the larger relative error of value and derivative; qualify_legendre.py:41 defines it.

    This supports error distributions and error versus degree/order/endpoint distance. Exclude the two overflow rows: their actual=null and relative_error=0 encode expected rejection, not zero numerical error.

  2. Analytic-zero cancellation and quadrature behavior: ebcm-l6-cancellation.json

    Top-level schema: native_profile, mpmath_digits, symmetry, results[]. Rows contain out, in, analytic_value, mpmath_absolute_value, mpmath_reflection_error, integral_of_absolute_integrand, epsilon_times_absolute_integral, upstream_default, upstream_tight, quadrature_warnings, native_by_quadrature_order.

    Eight selected entries are analytically zero by reflection symmetry, supported by 80-digit mpmath. One example has high-precision magnitude 5.91e-82, estimated double-precision cancellation scale 1.62e-10, upstream residual 6.60e-10, and native residuals 3.94e-10 / 1.63e-10 / 2.08e-10 at quadrature orders 48/96/192.

    Plot absolute residual versus quadrature order, alongside the cancellation scale. These values show a roundoff floor, not monotonic convergence. The artifact lacks source/native hashes and covers selected entries rather than whole-matrix accuracy.

  3. Physical conservation and paper reproduction: papers/qualification.json

    cpc.curves.sphere_array_above_slab contains grid[99], native[99][2], upstream[99][2], where columns are T, R. From the saved native arrays, max |T+R−1| = 3.6637e-15. That is a physical conservation residual; the separately stored 1.2323e-14 maximum native/upstream difference is implementation parity.

    Its convergence contains indices[5], original_order=3, refined_order=5, refined_native[5][2], and max_absolute_change=1.0979e-4. threshold_approach stores four additional two-sided wavelengths around 350 nm and max_power_balance_error=9.3301e-11. The exact singular endpoint is explicitly excluded.

    ebeam.curves.{sphere,cylinder} contains grid[50], native, upstream, and published_reference, each [50][2] with CL, EELS columns. Units are 1/eV for the sphere and 1/(eV nm) for the cylinder. Its five-point convergence stores refined values and relative changes: sphere order 4→6, maximum EELS change 0.002385; cylinder 12→14, maximum 0.006168. These are cutoff sensitivities.

    author_notebook_grid additionally preserves complete 200-point spectra. Author agreement, upstream parity, conservation, and cutoff sensitivity should have separate labels.

  4. Thermal author-reference agreement, symmetry, and convergence: thermal-result.json, backed by thermal-source.json

    rows[300] contains index, frequency_hz, author_absorption_um_squared, rust_absorption_um_squared, author_relative_error; 52 rows additionally contain upstream values and both upstream/native and upstream/author relative differences.

    Maximum author-reference relative difference is 0.0057665; median 1.9173e-7. angular_cuts[3] contains index, rust_values[200], author_max_relative_error, azimuth_invariance_relative_error, and helicity_symmetry_relative_error; maximum saved symmetry residual is 1.5584e-14.

    convergence[22] contains index, lmax, absorption_um_squared, covering five frequencies and cutoffs 6–16. Compare each cutoff with the highest saved cutoff, labeling this as truncation sensitivity.

    thermal-source.json embeds 300-point absorption/thermal spectra, polar_angles[200], angular emission arrays [200][3], material data [346][3], and author-source provenance. No external array files are required.

    thermal-upstream-comparison.json is a different native build, with 52 sampled rows, three angular cuts, and 12 convergence records. Do not merge its Rust observations into the fuller dataset.

  5. Saved browser cutoff sensitivity: browser/convergence.json

    Preserves wasmSha256, conventions, scope, and spherical[8], shell[6], practical[24], extended[4]. Each case has parameters and results[] by lmax; observables are scattering/extinction, coated/bare-core ratios, or values[]{angle,target,intensity}.

    Practical intensity changes from lmax 4→8 reach 39.31%. This supports an honest limitations/convergence plot. The artifact explicitly says higher cutoffs are comparators, not assumed converged truth.

Other material has narrower utility:

  • metasurface-convergence.json: 558 rows with columns radius, period, wavelength, angle_deg, R_lmax4, R_lmax6; maximum absolute difference 0.00320049. These are upstream treams 0.4.5 cutoff comparisons, not measured native error.
  • geometry-qualification.json and coefficient-qualification.json: hashes plus verified/failed path lists; sampled referenced outputs contain timing/RSS, not saved error arrays. Their pass counts cannot support accuracy plots.
  • WASM reference.json and inline high-precision test fixtures contain expected arrays, without captured native measurements.

Verified through source inspection and lightweight JSON parsing. No edits, renders, tests, builds, benchmarks, or Git changes.

items.html:
Three remaining issues:

  • P2 — Raw and scaled accuracy metrics are misclassified. plot_benchmarks.py:1114 relies on metric-name substrings. Paper passivity_nonnegative_violation and scattering_exceeds_extinction are raw differences with differing units, but get pooled and labeled dimensionless. Conversely, physics layer_split_scaled_absolute, divergence_scaled_absolute, and ewald_split_scaled_absolute divide by reference scales yet receive “raw workload units.” Collector evidence: qualify_paper_accuracy.py:261, qualify_physics.py:173. Use explicit classifications for these metrics.

  • P2 — Every FD trial inherits a passing status. plot_benchmarks.py:1083 marks every sweep/directional observation passed when overall validation passes. The harness gates the selected full-coordinate step and minimum directional error, not every trial (benchmark_gradients.py:423). Mark trial sweeps diagnostic and preserve selected-step/gate metadata.

  • P3 — Recorded high-precision errors appear “not measured.” plot_benchmarks.py:1215 uses that label for all null numeric errors. The reference collector deliberately preserves measured values outside float64 range in error_high_precision (qualify_references.py:325). Display that string before falling back to “not measured.”

The inspected live Mac path currently contains broad CPU results only, so gradient findings are source/schema based. No new timing-normalization issue found. No renders, tests, builds, benchmarks, edits, or Git changes.
